name: LOBA
description: Loba (Spanish for 'She-Wolf') is a popular Rummy-style card game widely played in Argentina, Bolivia, Uruguay, and across South America. Similar to Continental Rummy and Carioca, it is played over multiple rounds with increasing difficulty. Players aim to form specific combinations of 'Juegos' (Sets) and 'Escaleras' (Sequences). It is known for its fast pace and the inclusion of Jokers as powerful wildcards.

content.text: Loba (Spanish for 'She-Wolf') is a popular Rummy-style card game widely played in Argentina, Bolivia, Uruguay, and across South America. Similar to Continental Rummy and Carioca, it is played over multiple rounds with increasing difficulty. Players aim to form specific combinations of 'Juegos' (Sets) and 'Escaleras' (Sequences). It is known for its fast pace and the inclusion of Jokers as powerful wildcards.

Believed to have evolved from the Spanish game 'ChinchÃ³n' and the broader European 'Continental Rummy' family in the mid-20th century. The name 'Loba' evokes the 'wolfish' nature of stealing opponents' discards and the predatory approach to collecting cards.
Each player is dealt 11 cards (in some variants 13). The remaining cards form the stock pile. One card is turned up to start the discard pile.

items.text: Loba de Menos: Goal is to have the lowest total without going out; different scoring dynamic.
Loba de Mar: Coastal variant with specific rules about opening requirements and wild cards.
Carioca: The Chilean/Brazilian variant with fixed round-contracts (similar to Contract Rummy).
ChinchÃ³n: The 1-deck Spanish parent game, using 40 or 48 cards.
Loba de Mas: Variant with additional wild cards or modified opening requirements.
